question: Six times the present age of P exceeds the present age of Q by 11 years. After 10 years, three times Q’s age will be 27 years less than six times P’s age at that time. What is the present age (in years) of Q?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Let P and Q be the present ages.

From the first given condition, we have: 6P − Q = 11

From the second condition: 6(P + 10) − 3(Q + 10) = 27 ⇒ 6P − 3Q = −3

Since the term '6P' is common, simply subtract the second equation from the first to eliminate P.

⇒ (6P − Q) − (6P − 3Q) = 11 − (−3) ⇒ 2Q = 14 ⇒ Q = 7

**∴ The correct answer is 7 years.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Condition 1: Six times the present age of P exceeds the present age of Q by 11 years.

Condition 2: After 10 years, 3 times Q's age is 27 less than 6 times P's age.
